title: Ledger and Alibi
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Vane, the town's revered founder, is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, concierge Marguerite Dravenmoor's fifteen years of quietly cataloging guests, gossip, and grievances make her the only person who can reconstruct what really happened. Her investigation unearths a ledger of payments she herself once kept for a man who vanished — her brother, presumed dead in the same year Vane was buried. As the trial of the accused gravedigger approaches, Marguerite must decide whether exposing the truth will save an innocent man or destroy the fragile found family that took her in. In the end, she testifies to her own complicity, closes the case by finding her brother alive and hiding in plain sight as the hotel's night porter, and chooses memory over myth.
about_author: Sebastian Kavanagh is the pen name of a former hotel night auditor who spent a decade listening at the edge of other people's secrets. He writes mysteries about the people who keep places running and the pasts they file away.

chapters.title: The Exhumation
chapters.summary: Marguerite watches from the hotel steps as officials open Aldous Vane's grave and find it empty. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: cold shock beneath professional composure; her ordered world cracks open.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Keys
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: how Marguerite came to Bellhaven Hollow after her brother Tomas disappeared, and how she built her archive of the town's secrets. POV: Marguerite. Beat: grief disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Accused Gravedigger
chapters.summary: Wren Okafor, the young groundskeeper charged with disturbing the grave, insists he found it already empty. Marguerite, who trained him, believes him. POV: Wren. Beat: loyalty tested by fear.

chapters.title: Guest Register, 2009
chapters.summary: Marguerite pulls the old register from the year Vane died and finds a page razored out — a page she remembers handling. POV: Marguerite. Beat: dread; her own archive is compromised.

chapters.title: The Night Porter
chapters.summary: Marguerite notices small wrongnesses: the porter Ivor knows corridors he shouldn't, hums Tomas's childhood song. She dismisses it as coincidence. POV: Marguerite. Beat: uncanny longing.

chapters.title: Vane's Widow
chapters.summary: Eleanor Vane summons Marguerite privately, offering money to stop the investigation — and letting slip that the body was never Aldous's. POV: Eleanor. Beat: menace wrapped in civility.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: In her own handwriting, Marguerite finds entries recording payments to 'A.V.' from townsfolk buying silence about something in 2009. POV: Marguerite. Beat: horror at what she enabled without understanding.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: The prosecutor offers Wren a deal if he implicates someone; Wren refuses. Marguerite realizes the trial is a clock ticking on the truth. POV: Wren. Beat: stubborn integrity under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Town Swore
chapters.summary: Marguerite interviews elders who all repeat the same rehearsed story of Vane's death, word for word — evidence of coordinated memory. POV: Marguerite. Beat: unease at collective amnesia.

chapters.title: Ivor's Hands
chapters.summary: Marguerite traps Ivor with a detail only Tomas would know; he deflects, but his hands shake. She begins to hope and fears hoping. POV: Marguerite. Beat: trembling, dangerous hope.

chapters.title: The Fire
chapters.summary: The hotel's archive room burns; someone destroys the 2009 records. Marguerite saves one box — her private ledger. POV: Wren. Beat: loss, and the realization the truth has enemies.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Confession, Partial
chapters.summary: Eleanor admits she helped bury an empty coffin to protect the town's founding myth — and her son's inheritance. But she didn't act alone. POV: Eleanor. Beat: complicity dressed as devotion.

chapters.title: Found Family Fractures
chapters.summary: The hotel staff who raised Marguerite beg her to stop before the town turns on them all. She must weigh their safety against Wren's freedom. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Following ledger coordinates, Marguerite and Wren find an unmarked grave on Vane land containing a stranger's bones — the real occupant of the founder's plot. POV: Wren. Beat: grim vindication.

chapters.title: Who Signed
chapters.summary: The ledger's final page bears a signature Marguerite never questioned: her late mentor, the former concierge, who orchestrated the swap. POV: Marguerite. Beat: betrayal by the person who taught her everything.

chapters.title: Pre-Trial Motion
chapters.summary: The prosecutor moves to exclude the ledger as tainted; Marguerite's own past becomes the defense's weapon. She may have to testify. POV: Wren. Beat: cornered, escalating stakes.

chapters.title: Ivor Runs
chapters.summary: Ivor disappears the night before Marguerite can confront him, leaving behind Tomas's old watch. She understands: he is protecting her by staying hidden. POV: Marguerite. Beat: heartbreak sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Letters
chapters.summary: In the mentor's effects, Marguerite finds letters revealing why: Vane was dying and chose to vanish, trading his legend for the town's debts being paid — with her brother as witness. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the myth dismantled.

chapters.title: Climax: The Testimony
chapters.summary: At trial, Marguerite takes the stand, confesses her role keeping the ledger, and lays out the whole scheme — naming names, including her mentor's posthumous guilt and Eleanor's bargain. POV: Marguerite. Beat: cathartic exposure; she burns her own alibi to save Wren.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Wren is acquitted; charges shift to the surviving conspirators. The town reels as its founding story collapses. POV: Wren. Beat: justice arriving imperfectly, gratitude toward Marguerite.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Ivor returns, and on the empty midnight lobby floor, brother and sister finally speak — fifteen years of silence ending between the desk and the elevator. POV: Marguerite. Beat: reunion without absolution, love without erasure.

chapters.title: New Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite archives the case honestly, keeps the hotel, and begins a new register — recording truths instead of secrets. The town must live with its real history. POV: Marguerite. Beat: quiet resolution; memory chosen over myth.
